transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Dana Rivers (Redwood) -- Rohan Patel, Sophie Martens, Ben Caldwell, Terry Ng, Aisha Brown (Cardinal)
Link to artifacts: https://redwood.app/s/abc123/poc-deck , benchmark sheet: https://sheets.fake/cardinal-bench

Summary:
Quick sync to review latest pilot scorecard, dig into two regression clusters (prompt fidelity & hallucination around meter IDs), agree on triage plan and next steps for a VPC canary and security packet.

Topics:
- Scorecard deltas vs last week (precision drop on entity extraction)
- Prompt-set curation and negative examples
- Guardrail adjustments, failure modes and alert thresholds
- Private/VPC deploy gating and perf run

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We've got about 50 minutes, quick agenda. Luis will run through the scorecard, Terry will show the prompt diffs, and then we triage.
[00:24] Luis Ortega: Cool, um so looking at the numbers, overall accuracy is stable at 88% but entity precision for meter_id dropped from 94 to 81, most errors look like partial matches or swapped digits. Could be prompt drift or recent model patch.
[00:46] Rohan Patel: When you say model patch, do you mean the quantized variant you swapped in last week? I thought we were still on the baseline fp16.
[01:05] Luis Ortega: Right, good call. There was a fallback in the routing layer on Friday during peak where traffic hit the quantized q4b variant — might explain subtle tokenization differences. Also our prefix caching might be replaying an older prompt. We suspect kv cache behaviour — spelled out as k v cash in the logs sometimes.
[01:30] Terry Ng: I pulled the failing examples into the sheet, see rows 112-150. Many of them are short-form prompts where the model truncates leading zeros in meter ids e g '007824' -> '7824'.
[01:51] Sophie Martens: That's actually a product issue too; our downstream parser expects fixed-width. If the model drops leading zeros, the client rejects.
[02:06] Ben Caldwell: From infra side, I'm also seeing a slight latency bump on the dedicated pool when we run batch sizes above 8. We're still on the redwoood ded... Redwood Dedicated trial node but with a different kernel set, so could be kernel mismatch. Logs attached in the deck.
[02:33] Maya Chen: Thanks Ben. We'll run a perf test on the dev cluster with the quantized and non-quantized route and send you the config. Luis — can you sketch the targeted experiment now?
[02:44] Luis Ortega: Sure. Two arms: A baseline fp16 model pinned for this traffic, and a q4b quantized variant. We'll run 48 hours with production-like distribution, capture token-level differences and per-example diffs. Also we'll disable prefix caching for a subset to see if the KV-cache replay causes truncation. Capture both latency P95 and semantic diffs.
[03:10] Terry Ng: For scoring, can we use a stricter matcher on meter_id — exact match plus Levenshtein <= 1 as a fallback? Right now the scorer is fuzzy which accepts '7824' as match.
[03:28] Luis Ortega: Yes, we can tighten the scorer and add a post-processor that pads leading zeros if the pattern looks numeric and length mismatch. But we should also track hallucination cases where IDs are invented.
[03:46] Aisha Brown: Security question — if we enable VPC private deploy, is audit logging preserved and where does the telemetry flow? We need to confirm KMS integration and HSM options.
[04:05] Maya Chen: Short answer: yes, audit logs are preserved in Private mode and can be forwarded to your SIEM. KMS integration supported; HSM via partner. I'll share the detailed security pack after the call.
[04:23] Rohan Patel: Can we get a SOC2 attestation? Our procurement requires it before enabling dedicated.
[04:31] Maya Chen: Absolutely, sending SOC2 + ISO docs. I'll attach them to the CRM entry and to the shared drive.
[04:40] Dana Rivers: Quick note on guardrails — we added a new reject rule for 'invented meter id' patterns and a soft-fallback to request clarification from end user. It reduced bad outputs in staging by ~60%.
[05:03] Terry Ng: But it also increased user friction in some flows, we need to whitelist high-confidence cases.
[05:15] Sophie Martens: Could we add a confidence threshold per route? For billing flows it's stricter, for customer support it's softer.
[05:27] Luis Ortega: Yep, Redwood Console already supports per-route thresholds, we can map routes and set token-level thresholds. We'll propose tuned thresholds in the next artifact.
[05:40] Ben Caldwell: About the VPC canary — I'll need the deployment manifest and expected CIDR ranges, then I can set up peering. Also curious about egress patterns and whether the runtime will initiate outbound connections to telemetry endpoints.
[06:00] Maya Chen: We'll share a minimal manifest and the telemetry whitelist. Egress is optional and can be disabled; metrics can be pushed to your Prometheus push gateway if you prefer.
[06:18] Rohan Patel: One other regressed cluster is short-answer hallucinations where the model invents meter-location names. Any ideas on immediate guardrails?
[06:31] Luis Ortega: We can add a grounding check against a canonical table of known locations on-cardinal side. If the model emits a location not in the table, trigger review or fall back to 'unknown, please verify'. Also tighten generation temperature or force deterministic decoding for those routes.
[06:55] Terry Ng: I'll export the canonical location list and share. Also I'll mark examples in the sheet that should be exact-match only.
[07:10] Maya Chen: Great. Let's recap decisions and owners.
[07:16] Luis Ortega: Action: run 48h perf run comparing fp16 vs q4b with cache toggles — I own.
[07:24] Maya Chen: Action: send security pack + SOC2 + KMS details — I own.
[07:30] Terry Ng: Action: finalize golden prompt set and label negatives in the sheet — Terry owns.
[07:36] Ben Caldwell: Action: provision VPC peering and run canary cluster next Tue — Ben owns.
[07:42] Sophie Martens: Can we aim for an 80/20 rollback policy if the quantized variant crosses 5% delta on meter_id precision?
[07:53] Luis Ortega: Yep, we'll set automated rollback at that threshold in the routing policy.
[08:00] Rohan Patel: Timeline check: we need production-ready behavior in ~3 weeks for the mid-March pilot milestone. Is that realistic?
[08:12] Maya Chen: It's tight but doable if we run these experiments immediately and lock down prompt sets. We'll escalate support if we see blockers.
[08:22] Dana Rivers: I'll coordinate a security deep dive next week once Maya sends docs.
[08:30] Aisha Brown: Please include evidence of RBAC controls and audit log retention in the packet.
[08:36] Maya Chen: Will do.
[08:40] Luis Ortega: Any other questions?
[08:44] Terry Ng: One nit — sometimes the transcript shows 'SAM-el' for SAML in our notes, just FYI.
[08:52] Maya Chen: Haha noted.
[08:55] Ben Caldwell: Ok closing, I'll start the peering tickets.
[09:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, see you next Wednesday same time for triage check.

End of transcript.
